name: Posterolateral approach to the hip (periprosthetic)
corridor: Posterolateral split of gluteus maximus with detachment of the short external rotators and a posterior capsulotomy to reach the posterior hip and femur

positioning.text: Position in lateral decubitus with supports preventing rotation away from true lateral and padding at pressure points; prone positioning is also possible.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the posterior superior iliac spine, the greater trochanter, and the femoral shaft.

incision.text: Curve the incision toward the PSIS to a point about 6 cm proximal to the greater trochanter and extend it about 6 cm distally along the femoral axis.

superficial_interval.text: Incise the fascia lata and split the gluteus maximus in line with its fibers across the greater trochanter.

deep_interval.text: Place heavy stay sutures in the piriformis and conjoined obturator internus and gemelli, detach the short external rotators bluntly, and open a broad-based three-sided posterior capsulotomy.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, fascia lata, gluteus maximus, the short external rotators, and the posterior hip capsule.

structures_at_risk.text: The sciatic nerve lies just posterior to the short external rotators and must be protected, and its exposure is unnecessary for routine arthroplasty.

danger_zones.text: The interval deep to the short external rotators and quadratus femoris is the danger zone for the sciatic nerve.

retraction_hazards.text: Keep the hip extended and knee flexed and avoid deep posterior retraction that stretches the sciatic nerve.

exposure.text: Exposes the posterior hip, femoral head and neck, and proximal femur for arthroplasty or fracture fixation.

limitations.text: The posterior approach has a higher dislocation rate than anterior exposures unless the capsule and rotators are securely repaired.

indications.text: Indicated for revision hip arthroplasty and open reduction and internal fixation of periprosthetic femoral fractures.

closure.text: Repair the short external rotators and capsule through drill holes in the posterior greater trochanter, since secure repair reduces dislocation, then close in layers with a subfascial drain.

complications.text: Complications include posterior hip dislocation, sciatic nerve injury, and wound problems.

procedure_applications.condition: A periprosthetic femoral fracture or revision needs posterior exposure of the hip and femur
Revision hip arthroplasty is performed posteriorly

questions.question: Which nerve is most at risk in the posterolateral hip approach?
questions.answer: The sciatic nerve, lying just posterior to the short external rotators.

questions.question: What most reduces dislocation risk after a posterior approach?
questions.answer: Secure repair of the capsule and short external rotators.

questions.question: Which muscle is split to reach the short external rotators?
questions.answer: The gluteus maximus, in line with its fibers.
